newsitem.title: USA: FDA plans meetings to enforce smoking rules.
newsitem.headline: FDA plans meetings to enforce smoking rules.

text.p: Federal health officials said Monday they will hold nationwide town meetings to build support of new teen smoking regulations and will set up new ways of working with states to enforce the rules.

The first of the new Food and Drug Administration regulations, which strictly ban cigarette sales to minors, will go into effect this month. Other rules limiting advertising, vending machines and tobacco-related sponsorship of sports and entertainment events will be phased in later.
The rules were being challenged in court and one decisive case was being heard in Greensboro, N.C., Monday.

The 10 town meetings will involve merchants as well as health and community groups. "We want retailers to see how much people in their communities care, we want them to see how much grass roots support there is for these rules," FDA associate commissioner Sharon Natanblut told a meeting of health professionals.
The initial town meetings will be in Baltimore and Boston Tuesday.

Richard Barnes, an FDA official who works with state regulators, said the FDA will start in 10 states contracting with local enforcement agencies. Some of the arrangements may be nontraditional as the FDA tries to see which approaches work best before stepping up enforcement nationwide.

Businesses caught selling tobacco to youths under 18 will get a warning letter and a $250 fine on the second violation. The FDA will also send "positive reinforcement" letters to retailers that refuse to sell to minors, officials said.

In addition, the FDA is adding teen smoking information to its web page and has set up a toll-free line -- 888-FDA-4KIDS -- to get information about the regulations or to report retailers suspected of breaking the rules.
